title: Bird-Feeder Squirrel-Raid Detection
dataSources: BirdNET detections (`birdnet:detection`), trail-cam detections (`trailcam:detection`), moth-trap captures (`mothtrap:capture`), bat-detector passes (`batdetector:pass`), pollinator counts (`pollinator:count`), wildlife-cam visits (`wildlifecam:visit`).
app: Backyard wildlife monitoring — BirdNET acoustic bird ID, trail cameras with object detection, camera moth traps, ultrasonic bat detectors, and pollinator counts — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=wildlifecam:visit location=feeder
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(label="squirrel",1,0))) as raids, sum(eval(if(label="bird",1,0))) as birds by _time
| sort - _time
description: Counts squirrel raids on the bird feeder versus genuine bird visits, quantifying the eternal backyard battle.
value: Squirrels empty feeders fast; a daily raid count tells you whether a baffle is working and how much seed the squirrels steal.
implementation: Feed feeder-cam detections into `index=personal`; schedule daily and compare squirrel raids to bird visits.
visualization: Column chart of daily squirrel raids versus bird visits.
grandmaExplanation: It counts how often squirrels raid the bird feeder versus real bird visits, tracking that classic garden battle.
